title: Every Integration Boost Instance must pre-specify a Savings Rate Adjustment Strategy for handling changes to the Sky Savings Rate
content:
Among the required Initial Planning Document fields at A.2.2.9.2.2.3.1.3 is `Integration Boost Savings Rate Adjustment Strategy`, to be populated "with details for handling adjustments to Sky Savings Rate." It is one of only two fields the Prime Agent is expected to revise before GovOps review, one of two GovOps may amend during review (A.2.2.9.2.2.3.2.4.2.1), and it is carried into the ratified Instance Configuration Document at A.2.2.9.2.2.3.6.3.

The field exists because of what the Boost is. A.2.2.9.2.2.1.1 defines it as the Sky Savings Rate times unrewarded USDS balances — a payment whose size is set by a parameter Sky Governance controls and can move at any time. Without a pre-agreed rule, every SSR change would reopen every Integration Boost arrangement.

Making the strategy a **ratified Instance parameter** rather than an operational understanding means the rate-change behaviour is approved by token holders alongside everything else, and cannot be reinterpreted by either side afterwards. Partners get contractual clarity on how their yield responds to Sky's monetary decisions; Sky retains full freedom to change the SSR, because the propagation question was settled per instance in advance.

This is the Atlas's pre-established-method pattern applied to an economic parameter: the response to a foreseeable disruption is written before the disruption, so no party is negotiating under pressure when it arrives.
description: Because the Boost is defined as a multiple of a rate Sky can change, each instance ratifies in advance how a rate move propagates to the partner rather than renegotiating each time.
